title: The henselization of a pair is flat with the same quotients by powers of the ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal and $(A^h,I^h)$, $I^h=IA^h$, the henselization of the pair $(A,I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], with structure map $\eta:A\to A^h$. Then $\eta$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and for every $n\ge1$ the ring map $A/I^n\to A^h/I^nA^h$ induced by $\eta$ is an isomorphism (note $I^nA^h=(I^h)^n$).

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGU (lemma-henselization-flat, line 3105) and its proof (étale maps are flat, Algebra Lemma Tag 00U2; filtered colimits of flat modules are flat, Algebra Lemma Tag 05UT lemma-colimit-flat; $A/I^n\to B/I^nB$ isomorphisms by flatness, Algebra Lemma Tag 051H; colimit over the category of [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization])

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization] to obtain essential smallness, filteredness and a colimit d whose canonical quotient map modulo I is bijective.

Each stage is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-ind-flat] and Mathlib ObjectProperty.of_essentiallySmall_index to the given colimit presentation in Under A. This proves flatness of its structure map.

The unique isomorphism d.pt to c.pt between colimit vertices is an isomorphism in Under A, so its underlying ring equivalence e satisfies e composed with the structure map of d equals the structure map of c. Ideal.map_map identifies the extended ideals. Ideal.quotientEquiv gives an equivalence between the two quotients, and the canonical quotient map for c is its composite with the canonical quotient map for d. Hence it is bijective.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-iso-mod-ideal-powers] to the colimit structure map, using its flatness and the bijectivity modulo I just established. This proves bijectivity modulo every positive power without a separate quotient-colimit argument.
